sections.html:
H. compressa is a sleeper goby that lives free swimming in the water column. In contrast to many other gobies this fish is not a bottom dweller. Common name: Empire gudgeon.

Available size: 4–5 cm. Origin: Indonesia.
The species occurs in the wild in northern Australia and southern New Guinea.
The fish are extremely hardy and undemanding. They tolerate temperatures between 18 and 35°C and almost any water chemistry. However, medium hard water will fit best.

In Germany the genus Hypseleotris is called "minnow goby", because the fish live like schooling minnows in the open water. It is highly recommended to keep several males together in one tank, so at least one is in the mood to show the fantastic colours.
Males literally switch the light on while displaying. The females are not so deep bodied and have a rather dull coloration.

Sadly it is very difficult to breed this fish under aquarium conditions. The fish spawn readily (they are substrate brooders), but the eggs and the fry are extremely small and the offspring is able to survive only in strong brackish or marine water. Here they can be fed with live marine plankton (for example oyster larvae).
Lexicon: Hypseleotris: ancient Greek, means "deep Eleotris"; Eleotris is another genus of goby. compressa: Latin, means "compressed".
